summary: Discovery call with Sentinels Analytics to evaluate where to host embeddings and rerank: hosted Redwood API, Dedicated reserved capacity, or Private VPC/on-prem. Key constraints: high throughput (target ~500 qps), EU data residency and SOC2, current stack uses ES + FAISS sidecar, interested in hybrid search with rerank. Agreed to run a 6-week pilot with benchmarking and security review.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2029-04-02 14:30 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Priya Kumar (Sentinels - Head of Search), Tom Hale (Sentinels - Infra Lead), Marta Novak (Sentinels - ML Eng)
---
[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you making time. Quick intro — I'm Avery, I'll be your AE. Diego's our SE, he'll jump into perf stuff. Priya, Tom, Marta — thanks for being here.
[00:23] Priya: Yeah thanks, hi, um yeah quick context — Sentinels runs a relevance stack over customer support docs and product data, about 20M docs, currently an ElasticSearch frontend with FAISS for vector fanout, we do a lightweight cross-encoder rerank for top-10. We're exploring replacing the FAISS sidecar with a managed vector path and maybe move rerank to hosted inference.
[01:05] Diego: cool, thanks. can you tell us the SLOs and typical QPS?
[01:12] Priya: Target is around 400 to 600 QPS at peak — average closer to 220. Tail matters a lot, p95 ideally under 120ms for the embedding+search+rerank path, p99 under 250 if possible. We're sensitive to cost though, so we look for predictable unit economics.
[01:47] Tom: Also note we have EU data residency requirements for a subset of projects and SOC2 audit soon. So anything that touches PII needs to be auditable.
[02:05] Avery: Got it, thanks. high level, we can run you on Redwood Hosted API to start — fastest time to value — or Redwood Dedicated for reserved GPU pools if you need throughput predictability, or Private (VPC/on-prem) for strict residency and audit controls. Diego, do you want to frame the perf tradeoffs?
[02:30] Diego: Sure. For retrieval+rerank there's a couple axes — where you serve embeddings (hosted vs local vector DB), dimensionality choices (we commonly see 1536 vs 768 vs compact 256 depending on fidelity), and whether you do hybrid search (annonser style lexical + vector) before rerank. Hosted endpoint lowers ops but network hop adds latency, Dedicated lowers tail by avoiding noisy neighbors, Private gives full control for compliance but needs infra ops. Quantization (4-bit/8-bit) can save cost and fit models on less-capacity but may impact embedding fidelity slightly — depends on eval.
[03:25] Marta: On the embeddings, we currently use 1536 dims from an open encoder, storage is already heavy — 20M x 1536 is non-trivial. We estimated shard sizes and we're worried about fanout cost when we do topk 100 and rerank.
[03:51] Priya: yeah, so we were thinking: can we do a hybrid topk-40 lexical + topk-200 vector then rerank top-20? what's realistic?
[04:05] Diego: That's a common pattern. With Redwood's smart routing and prefix caching we can reduce duplicate compute — e.g., keep a warmed kv cache for frequent queries. For hosting: if you choose Hosted we recommend caching and small batching to keep p95 down; Dedicated can be tuned for continuous batching heavier throughput.
[04:28] Tom: Security question — if we move embeddings to hosted, where does data live? Can you sign a DPA and enforce EU region only? Also KMS for keys?
[04:45] Avery: Yes, Hosted supports region pinning to EU regions for data residency, we have DPA templates, and Redwood integrates with customer KMS (we support common providers and HSM integrations on Private). We'll share the SOC2 pack and the data flow diagrams.
[05:10] Priya: Great. On benchmarks — what would you run to show parity with our FAISS pipeline?
[05:20] Diego: We typically run a throughput sweep and an accuracy eval. For throughput: 10k representative queries with realistic QPS shape (bursts) and measure p50/p95/p99 both for cold and warm KV cache. For accuracy: rerank NDCG, precision@k vs your current cross-encoder. We'll provide a harness and sample configs — there is a small noise in transcription here — the repo link is in chat.
[06:00] Marta: Can you quantize embeddings? We saw people do 256-d compact embeddings and get decent results but wonder if Redwood's runtime handles sparse/compact dims well.
[06:12] Diego: Yep, runtime supports mixed precision and we have quantization profiles — recommended path is to eval fidelity drop vs cost saving. In some customer cases, 256-d distilled embeddings with a small reranker produced near identical user facing relevance and ~3x cost reduction.
[06:42] Priya: If we go Dedicated, does that mean we have dedicated GPU pools for embedding gen and for rerank separately? Or do you multiplex?
[06:52] Avery: You can carve pools by model/route. Many customers separate heavy rerank endpoints (cross-encoders) from embedding gen to avoid noisy neighbors. Autoscaling policies let you burst but within reserved capacity.
[07:10] Tom: Ops — if we want Private in our VPC, how much operator work is needed? We have an infra team but limited time.
[07:20] Diego: Private requires more setup — networking, EKS/VMs or our on-prem package. We provide a private control plane and templates, but you'll need to manage nodes, KMS integration and backups. We usually estimate a 2–4 week ops runway for an initial deploy with our onboarding support.
[07:45] Priya: Timeline — we're aiming to pick a vendor by end of Q2 and run a pilot in Q3. Budget is TBD but we'd like a predictable committed spend if Dedicated.
[08:00] Avery: Noted. Let's talk numbers briefly — for Hosted you pay per token for generation and per-embedding unit for vector ops, while Dedicated is reserved monthly with predictable throughput discounts. I'll share a comparative sheet.
[08:20] [00:08:20] Marta: real quick — on hybrid search, how do you handle lexical + vector scoring? Is that on the client side or inside Redwood routing?
[08:32] Diego: We leave the scoring flexible — many customers do lexical filtering in ES and then call Redwood for vector embed and a rerank, others push everything into Redwood's routing layer that can orchestrate calls to a VDB and a reranker. There's also built-in support for per-route weighting so you can tune lexical vs dense.
[09:05] Priya: Any case studies with similar scale — 20M docs, EU regs?
[09:12] Avery: We recently worked with a EU-based fintech (redacted) that used Dedicated + Private mix: embeddings hosted in EU, rerank on Dedicated; they passed SOC2 audits and kept audit logs. We'll include anonymized notes.
[09:40] Tom: What's the expected cost delta vs our FAISS ops? We currently run FAISS on spot instances and it's cheap per month but we handle ops ourselves.
[09:55] Diego: Typically you trade some raw VM cost for reduced engineering burden and unit economics predictability — we can run a TCO comparison. If you want minimal change, a hybrid approach (keep FAISS but push rerank to Dedicated) can give quick wins.
[10:18] Priya: For the rerank model, we currently host a small cross-encoder on GPU — can Redwood run custom models?
[10:26] Diego: Yes, you can bring-your-own-model (BYOM) and we support containerized models for Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports a curated model catalog and some customer models with vetting. For BYOM on Hosted we usually start with Dedicated or Private because of security and model artifacts.
[10:50] Marta: about embedding storage — if we host embeddings in your managed vector DB, how is retention and deletes handled for GDPR?
[10:58] Avery: We support retention policies and deletes; for EU data with GDPR you can choose Private or ensure Hosted has region pinning and deletion hooks. We'll share the deletion SLA.
[11:20] Priya: Ok practical pilot — what would you need from us to start a 6-week pilot?
[11:28] Diego: sample doc corpus (or a slice), query set (5–10k), target SLOs, and any privacy constraints. We'll run a baseline with your existing model and a Redwood config, produce perf and relevance delta, and propose a hosting plan.
[11:45] Priya: We'll do that. Also want to understand telemetry — can we get token-level cost breakdown and per-route latencies?
[11:55] Avery: Yes Redwood Console exposes per-route metrics, token costs, tracing hooks and error breakdowns. We can enable longer retention for enterprise.
[12:08] [00:12:08] Marta: Minor note — sometimes transcripts call your product 'Redwood inference' — we want exact product names for docs.
[12:18] Avery: thanks, we'll be careful.
[12:25] Priya: Any vendor lock-in concerns if we go with Dedicated?
[12:30] Diego: Dedicated is largely our managed runtime but you still control your models and data; Private is the least lock-in. We support export tooling for embeddings and model checkpoints.
[12:45] Tom: Network egress — if embeddings are hosted and vector DB calls go across region, what's the latency impact?
[12:53] Diego: That's why region pinning is important. For EU workloads, pinning to EU reduces egress and latency. We'll also run region-specific perf tests.
[13:12] [00:13:12] Priya: On dimensioning — any rule of thumb for dims vs throughput?
[13:18] Diego: Higher dims = larger KV footprint and slower nearest neighbor ops; if throughput is critical, smaller dims with a stronger reranker often wins. Rule: measure quality-vs-cost via an A/B eval. We'll include a recommended sweep (256, 768, 1536).
[13:42] Priya: Good. Could you briefly outline the pilot success criteria?
[13:48] Avery: Sure: 1) relevance parity within X% of your current NDCG (you define X), 2) p95 end-to-end latency < 120ms under target QPS, 3) predictable cost estimate for steady state, 4) security/compliance acceptance. If these hit, move to committed Dedicated or Private.
[14:10] Tom: When we run the perf harness, do you want us to include heavy fanout cases? We often do topk 200 and then rerank top 40.
[14:18] Diego: Yes include fanout patterns and burst shapes. Also include cold cache runs. We'll report cache hit rates and advise on prefix caching.
[14:35] [00:14:35] Priya: Okay, logistics — who will set up the test S3 and access?
[14:40] Tom: I can provision a pre-signed bucket. Marta will drop corpus and queries.
[14:45] Avery: Perfect. We'll also schedule a 1-hour kickoff for the pilot and share the scope doc.
[14:55] Marta: Are we able to run a quick smoke test with Hosted before committing to Dedicated?
[15:00] Diego: Absolutely, Hosted is fastest — we can do a smoke with small sample. If latency looks good, we move to Dedicated to optimize for tail.
[15:12] Priya: Anything else on compliance we should flag? We're doing SOC2 Type II and have a legal checklist.
[15:20] Avery: We'll route that to our security team and match items: encryption at rest, KMS, audit logs, SSO (SAML), RBAC. We'll include a compliance mapping doc.
[15:40] Tom: Also curious about cost modeling for dedicated — is there a published price sheet for reserved pools?
[15:48] Avery: I'll send the committed capacity pricing and example TCO scenarios.
[16:00] [00:16:00] Quick recap and close
Avery: Recap — action items: we'll send security pack and pricing, Diego will share benchmark plan and test harness, Priya/Tom will supply corpus and queries, schedule pilot kickoff. Next call: pilot kickoff tentative next Wednesday, 14:00 UTC.
Priya: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
Tom: thanks.
Marta: thanks.
Diego: thanks, bye.
Avery: Bye.
